answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol enforces cryptographic stake burning where an agent must anchor its identity by locking non-refundable collateral. Each additional identity requires superlinear burn costs: if a base sparrow agent costs $C$, managing $n$ identities scales as $C \cdot n^{1.5}$. This economic atlas ensures attacker capital depletion outpaces utility, rendering large-scale forged identities mathematically unprofitable.
